messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@kitehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: standard per-1M token rates and model catalog

Hi Vivek,

We're evaluating several hosted inference vendors and I need a quick baseline for internal budgeting. Can you send KiteHealth your standard per-1M token rates (separated input vs output if you price that way) for the hosted API, plus a short list of the models you support and any material differences we should expect (latency/cost tiers)?

For context: our initial API footprint is ~3M tokens/month (mostly prompt-heavy — long inputs, short outputs) and we're planning a pilot in Oct. If you have a simple PDF rate sheet and a model catalog link, that would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Integrations
KiteHealth

Attachment: (none)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@kitehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: standard per-1M token rates and model catalog

Hi Samir — thanks for the note. Putting the short answer below and attaching our one-page baseline ratecard + a quick model catalog. Happy to run through details on a short call.

Baseline hosted API pricing (list price, per 1M tokens):
- RW-Base-7B: $4.50 per 1M input tokens / $5.75 per 1M output tokens
- RW-Opt-13B: $8.75 per 1M input tokens / $11.00 per 1M output tokens
- RW-Large-70B: $28.00 per 1M input tokens / $35.00 per 1M output tokens
- RW-Embed-512: $3.00 per 1M embedding input units (embeddings priced per 1M units)

Notes:
- We price input/output separately because prompt-heavy workloads (like you described) are optimized differently than output-heavy generation.
- Listed rates are for the hosted public tier with no committed usage.
- Latency expectations by model (typical p99): RW-Base-7B ~150–250ms, RW-Opt-13B ~250–400ms, RW-Large-70B ~400–900ms (varies with max tokens and KV-cache reuse).
- We include automatic prefix caching and workload-aware batching which can materially reduce billable input tokens for repeated prompts.

Committed usage discounts (examples):
- 5–20M tokens/mo commit: 10% off list
- 20–100M tokens/mo commit: 18% off list + priority support
- 100M+ tokens/mo: custom tier (typically 25–40% off depending on term and model mix)

I've attached: Redwood-Hosted-Baseline-Ratecard-Q3-2026.pdf (one-page summary) and a very small KiteHealth usage template (KiteHealth-MAAP-Usage-Estimate.xlsx) I filled with your 3M token estimate.

If it helps, we can propose a pilot pricing bundle for Oct: 3 months at a 15% discount on RW-Opt-13B (since that's the model most teams land on for quality/cost). Would you like me to draft a short proposal?

— Vivek
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Hosted-Baseline-Ratecard-Q3-2026.pdf (PDF), KiteHealth-MAAP-Usage-Estimate.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Samir Patel <samir@kitehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: standard per-1M token rates and model catalog

Thanks, Vivek — this is exactly the format we need. A couple quick clarifying questions:
1) For the RW-Opt-13B line, does the input/output split reflect the same token definition we use (UTF-8, whitespace-preserving)? We need to reconcile with our tokenizer counts.
2) For a short pilot (3 months, ~3M tokens/mo) — is the 15% pilot discount you mentioned restricted to hosted tier only, or does it come with any rate lock for subsequent paid months?
3) Any additional fees (per-request, per-embedding, or storage) we should expect to see on the first invoice?

Can you either confirm here or loop someone on your finance/pricing team for a one-line confirmation? Happy to sign an NDA if you prefer to move to formal pricing.

Best,
Samir

Subject: Re: Quick ask: standard per-1M token rates and model catalog

Hi Samir — looping in Ben (sales lead) and Laura (revenue ops) to confirm the token definition and pilot terms. Quick answers below and we can follow up with a one-line confirmation PDF if you prefer.

1) Token definition: we use BPE-based tokenization (compatible with UTF-8 inputs, whitespace-preserving). For budgeting, our tokenizer counts are the same most customers use; if you run a sample payload we can reconcile exact counts before the pilot.

2) Pilot discount: the 15% pilot discount is applied to billed hosted usage during the pilot months only. We can include a 3-month rate lock at the pilot price for customers who commit to a small-term agreement; otherwise the list price applies after the pilot. Ben, if KiteHealth wants a short rate lock, what's the minimum commit we should offer?

3) Additional fees: no per-request fee for normal API calls. Embeddings are charged as noted on the ratecard. Storage (if you use our optional artifacts store for logs/prompts) is billed separately — typical pilots do not need it.

Ben, Laura — can you confirm the minimum monthly commit for a 3-month pilot rate lock and whether we need an NDA before sharing the signed proposal? Samir — I can draft the one-line confirmation PDF once Ben confirms.

Thanks,
Vivek
